test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 16 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The presence of which of the following soils in the hilly areas of South India makes the region suitable for tea and coffee cultivation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Laterite soil.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Laterite Soil**

__
 
• **The tea plant **grows well in** deep and fertile well-drained laterite soil, rich in humus and organic matter, coupled with tropical and sub-tropical climates.**
 
• **Laterite soils are good for tea, coffee and cashew cultivation.**
 
• This soil is **rock type rich in iron and aluminum.**
 
• It is commonly considered to have **formed in hot and wet tropical areas.**
 
• It is when wet are as soft as butter but **become hard and cloddy on drying.**
 
• They are particularly** found on high flat erosion surfaces in areas of high and seasonal rainfall.**
 
• They are **commonly found in the hilly areas of Orissa and Assam, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, and Kerala. **
 
• **These soils are reddish-brown in color due to the presence of iron oxide.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**Alluvial soil**

 
• **Alluvial soil is one of the best soils**, requiring the least water due to its high porosity.
 
• The **consistency of alluvial soil ranges from drift sand and rich, loamy soil to silt clays.**
 
• **India is one of the richest countries in the world in terms of alluvial soil,** which **covers more than 46% of its total land area.**
 
• Alluvial soils **remove sediments and nutrients flowing in the adjacent water.**
 
• They can also** remove other contaminants from rivers and improve water quality for downstream communities.**
 
• All alluvial soils **form by flooding.**

**Black soil**

 
• **Black soils are mineral soils **which have a black surface horizon, **enriched with organic carbon.**
 
• This soil is a **derivative of trap lava and are spread mostly across interior Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh on the Deccan lava plateau and the Malwa Plateau.**
 
• It is **fine textured and clayey in nature.**
 
• It has **high amounts of lime, iron, magnesium and generally low quantities of phosphorus, nitrogen and organic matter.**
 
• It is **black in colour** since it is formed from weathered lava rocks.

**Arid soil**

 
• **Arid soils are formed from the fragmentation of adjacent rocks** and are largely blown from Indus valley area and coastal regions.
 
• They mainly can be seen developing **western Rajasthan.**
 
• It mainly ranges from** red to brown in colour.**
 
• **It is generally sandy to gravelly in texture, **and have a high percentage of soluble salts.
 
• Due to the absence of vegetation and dry climate, it comprises a small percentage of organic matter.
